title: The families: document, key-value, wide column, graph and time series

videos.script: NoSQL is not one kind of database. It is everything that is not relational, and the families under that name disagree with each other more than with Postgres. {{families}} So this lesson takes one thing and stores it five ways. Ana Ribeiro orders two USB-C cables and a wireless mouse. Order 1001, 268.80 reais. {{order}} A relational database splits it across four tables and joins them back on every read. {{relational}} MongoDB keeps the whole order as one document, lines inside, and still reads every field. {{document}} Redis files it under a key. The value is bytes it never reads, so the key is the only way in. {{keyvalue}} Cassandra puts each line in a partition for Ana, sorted by date. Ask it a question the table was not built for, and it refuses, by name. {{widecolumn}} Then two families you will not install. A graph store follows links, for questions measured in hops. A time-series store keeps measurements, and throws the old ones away on purpose. {{graph}} Watch two things in every store. What one read hands back. And whether the server can see inside it. {{question}} Everything else in this course follows from those two answers.
